scenes.heading: Pipeline Design
scenes.narration: Good pipeline design turns messy source data into reliable, timely datasets through well-structured stages.

scenes.heading: Principles of solid pipelines
bullets: Idempotency: reruns produce the same result.
Observability: logs, metrics, and lineage throughout.
Recoverability: failures resume without corrupting data.
scenes.narration: Idempotent steps let you safely rerun a pipeline after a failure without creating duplicates. Modular stages are easier to test and reuse than one giant script. Observability shows you what happened, and recoverability means a hiccup never leaves data half-written.

scenes.heading: A typical batch pipeline
scenes.narration: Data first flows out of source systems and lands untouched in a raw zone, which preserves an auditable copy. Transformations then clean, join, and reshape it, with validation guarding quality. Only trusted output reaches the serving layer that analysts and applications consume.

scenes.heading: ETL vs ELT
scenes.narration: ETL transforms data before loading, which suited systems with limited storage and rigid schemas. ELT loads raw data first and transforms it inside a powerful warehouse or lake. Cloud compute has made ELT popular because it keeps raw data available and lets you reshape it on demand.

scenes.text: Well-designed pipelines are idempotent, modular, observable, and recoverable, so they deliver trustworthy data even when things go wrong.
scenes.narration: Design for failure from the start, and your pipelines will keep flowing reliably long after the first happy-path run.
